failedAssertions.reason: POST /api/streams/{id}/start returned HTTP 500 with the known supervisor available-list error instead of converging to a healthy live state.
After the underlying managed process exited, POST /api/streams/{id}/stop returned HTTP 500 (removed process group) instead of a stopped status payload.

The managed runner did not emit its heartbeat file automatically; only a manually injected stale heartbeat triggered a recoverable error, and the scheduled recovery then hit the same supervisor available-list failure.
Backend restart preserved one live record, but the required follow-up control action still failed with HTTP 500 from POST /api/streams/{id}/stop.
Scheduled start attempts failed with the supervisor available-list error and the one-shot schedule window expired without the stream ever reaching a live state.

Daily-quota exhaustion did not fail closed: API start still returned the supervisor available-list 500, and manual continuation showed quota-triggered SIGINTs followed by supervisor auto-restarts instead of a terminal stopped/error quota state.
After backend restart, status reconciled to one running record but the log surface was empty around the restart window and the follow-up stop control still returned HTTP 500.

blockedAssertions.blockedBy: The disabled-destination denial passed, but the enable-then-start success path was not completed in batch A and depends on the failing managed-runtime start surface.
No API-only live-state mutator exists, and the batch that owned this assertion did not start a managed stream to create the live scheduling-conflict precondition.
The missing-log branch passed, but no stream exposed real log content for raw-vs-important comparison without relying on the failing managed-runtime start path.

appliedUpdates.description: Added runtime-hardening API flow-validator guidance for the 8000/8001 validation split, serialized runtime mutations, and local MediaMTX destination usage.
Documented that a managed-runtime start returning a supervisor available-list 500 is a product failure to record during validation rather than a validator setup mistake.
